footnote: Source: company releases and calls (Jan to Jul 2026), Amazon's $220bn via Fortune (Jul 2026). Company basis, range midpoints
notes: Guidance went one way. Alphabet started 2026 at $175bn to $185bn in February, moved to $180bn to $190bn in April and to $195bn to $205bn in July. Meta went from $115bn to $135bn in January to $125bn to $145bn in April, then narrowed to $130bn to $145bn in July. Amazon said about $200bn in February and about $220bn in July because memory got dearer. That figure was given on the call, and we confirmed it through Fortune's report. Microsoft's April plan for calendar 2026 was about $190bn, about $25bn of it from higher component prices. In July it became about $175bn because some future leases were reclassified from finance to operating leases, and management said the investment plan had not changed, so it is not a cut. The four now total $720bn to $745bn, a midpoint of about $732.5bn, 79% above 2025. Take first-half spending away from full-year guidance and the four need about $210bn to $222bn a quarter in the second half, 23% to 31% more than the roughly $170bn of Q2 on the company basis.
